thread:
ryan: quick handoff — i'm stepping off in 10. Primary = ryan, Secondary = jen. There's a small coverage hole from 03:30-04:15 UTC while maya is on call transfer.

ryan: summary: earlier today we had transient errors hitting the routing layer for model assignments. Incident bot created INC-2024-112 at 1717521000 but that got auto-resolved after the hotfix. No customer-facing errors since 02:40 UTC.

incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-2024-112 created by monitor: routing-service-high-error-rate. Severity: P2. Affected: ~0.2% of requests, increased latency. Link: <https://redwood-internal/ops/incidents/INC-2024-112>.

jen: noted. Thanks for papering this down. Are there any remaining mitigation steps we need to keep watch on over the handoff window?

ryan: main ask — keep an eye on model-assignment errors and the fallback throttle rate. If errors creep above 1% for 10 minutes, escalate.

ryan: paging/escalation rules (repeat for clarity):
- If error rate for routing-service > 1% sustained for 10m => page SRE pager (pager: #sre-pager).
- If error rate > 5% OR customer-impacting user-facing failures start => escalate to ops lead (maya) and alert product.
- If latency tail > 2s increase for > 15m => page perf-oncall (sam).

ryan: quick runbook pointers: follow runbook: Routing-Service Quick Triage (RB-03). Steps to follow:```
1) Check routing-service logs: /var/log/routing/*.log on prod-router nodes
2) curl the health endpoints: curl -sS http://prod-router-1.internal/_health | jq
3) Look for KV-cache misses and assignment rejections
4) If assignment loop detected, trigger fallback: POST /admin/fallback?mode=soft
```

jen: got it. Where's the runbook link?

ryan: link -> <https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/RB-03-routing-quick-triage>. Also poster note: if you hit the fallback endpoint, annotate the incident with the command and rollback plan.

maya: i'm taking the escalation lead if this becomes customer impacting. If paged, i will coordinate the canary rollback plan and orchestrate the cross-team bridge.

sam: i'll own perf pages. If you see tail spikes, ping me and i'll open a perf bridge.

jen: OK. for the coverage gap between 03:30-04:15 UTC — ryan do you want to keep you as primary until 03:40 then jen covers?

ryan: yes, i'll extend primary to 03:45 and then jen you become primary. Secondary will be sam during that 03:45-04:15 window. I'll post a tidy summary before stepping off.

incident-bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance window 1717528800-1717532400 (model-variant-refresh) — this overlaps later with the 04:00 UTC deploy plan; any changes should be coordinated.

jen: noted re maintenance. i'll suppress non-urgent alerts during that window but keep SRE pager active.

ryan: last quick checklist before i leave:
- confirm all alerts routed to #sre-pager -> done
- escalate matrix pinned in thread -> done
- active incident logs archived under INC-2024-112 -> done

sam: thumbs up. thanks for the clear handoff.

maya: thanks — i'll be reachable via pager and DM. call if anything looks off. :phone: :warning:

jen: ack. i'll take over at 03:45 UTC and will post a status update on milestone (03:55).

ryan: handing off now. thanks team. :raised_hands:
